_note: Bloc proposals, V1.3d. Shaped after the real Stability and Growth Pact and the Excessive Deficit Procedure, but the numbers are game numbers set by tools/bloc_probe.gd and not by the Treaties -- see docs/bloc-model.md. File order is the council's agenda: src/sim/bloc.gd rotates an index over the loaded list, so a proposal added here changes what comes up and when. V3.3 re-measured the council over 27 members: the authored positions produced unanimous or near-unanimous divisions in which no member's abstention could matter, so debt_reduction_rule's position was re-set by tools/ (the tally probe) to land the division inside the player's pivotal band -- 385 for of 639 cast against a 351.45 threshold, so France's 81 seats decided it whichever way they voted. That was V3.3. Under V4.5b, NLD sponsors it and lobbies at the opening, and table T measures it carrying alone: 623 for with France, 542-97 abstaining, 542-178 against. The sweep reads carries-alone on every cell. It is the frugal members' rule now, not France's to decide. V4.5b gave each row a sponsor and a decision class, and placed both by tools/council_probe.gd's table T rather than by feel. stability_pact (DEU, the 1997 pact's champion) and debt_reduction_rule (NLD, the frugal file) stay qualified majority. minimum_corporate_rate is UNANIMITY, because EU tax law is (Art. 115 TFEU), and its floor moved from 18 to 15: 15 percent is the real Pillar Two floor (Council Directive (EU) 2022/2523, adopted by unanimity after a holdout). The move was forced by measurement as well. At 18 the four low-rate members (BGR, CYP, HUN, IRL) vetoed at every position on the sweep grid and under every sponsor, which is a treaty nobody could ever carry. At 15 two vetoes remain, BGR and HUN, the fight the real directive had. The sponsor is DEU, not FRA: France is the player, a player-sponsored row gets no AI lobbying, and with France as sponsor CYP and IRL stay against. The seven V4.5b rows were each placed by `--sweep`. Unanimity rows sit at the cell with the fewest vetoes, never more than three. The rows are ordered so the rotation never runs three rules in a row. This file holds seven rules and three money rows, so pairs of rules are unavoidable. Since 2026-10-15 the order is: two rules, a fund, two rules, a fund, two rules, a fund, one rule. union_policy.json's opening fund follows that last rule. own_resource_digital (FRA) calls 0.04, not the provisional 0.05: at 0.05 four members vetoed even at the best cell, and at 0.04 three do (CZE, POL, ROU). corporate_rate_high_floor runs at severity 0.10 and tolerance 10, with DEU as sponsor rather than FRA. Under France it drew at least six vetoes on every cell, because France does not lobby. Under DEU three remain: BGR, CYP, HUN. fiscal_compact_strict keeps the treaty's 60 percent but reads it over a tolerance of 100, at severity 0.15. At tolerance 60 seven or eight members vetoed on every cell. AUT sponsors it, the plan's choice. AUT is above 60 itself and vetoed its own proposal until the sponsor rule of 2026-10-15. GRC and ITA veto it, the two members furthest over. The same ruling moved stability_pact: DEU's 96 seats now vote for it whatever DEU appraises, so it carries alone on every cell of the grid. It is no longer the player-pivotal row V3.3 placed, and the eu's pivotal qualified-majority row is defence_industry_fund. vat_floor and joint_borrowing_facility carry with France's vote and fail without it. eurozone_fiscal_capacity calls 0.08 and draws three vetoes (CZE, POL, ROU), the members outside the euro. expenditure_ceiling carries on every cell of the grid: it binds nobody today.

proposals.name: Stability and Growth Pact
proposals.summary: Members undertake to hold the general government deficit under 3% of GDP. The Commission reports on those who do not, and the Council may levy a penalty.

proposals.name: Debt Reduction Rule
proposals.summary: A member carrying debt above 90% of GDP commits to a path back below it. The path is not enforced; the reporting is -- and the sponsorship is the green-liberal benches, whose fiscal hawkery is the debt brake's natural home in this council.

proposals.name: Digital Levy Own Resource
proposals.summary: A levy on the largest digital platforms' turnover, paid into the common budget rather than any member's. The bloc gains a revenue line of its own; every treasury that hosts a platform's European office loses the argument it used to win.

proposals.name: Minimum Corporate Rate
proposals.summary: A floor under corporation tax across the bloc, so that no member can compete for headquarters by cutting below it.

proposals.name: VAT Rate Floor
proposals.summary: A standard VAT rate of at least 15% in every member. Every member is above it today; the floor exists so that nobody races down to it tomorrow.

proposals.name: Joint Borrowing Facility
proposals.summary: The bloc borrows again on its own name and lends the proceeds on to members at its own rate. The cheap money arrives now; the question of who stands behind it is left for a later council.

proposals.name: Corporate Rate Convergence
proposals.summary: A second, higher floor under corporation tax: 21%, closer to the large members' own rates than to the small ones'. The tax competition the first floor narrowed, this one would end.

proposals.name: Expenditure Ceiling
proposals.summary: Total public [g=spending]spending[/g] held under 50% of GDP. The ceiling does not touch what a government spends on; it touches how much, which is the argument the frugal members have always wanted to have.

proposals.name: Common Fiscal Capacity
proposals.summary: A standing budget line that pays out when a member's economy turns down, funded by a call on all of them. Insurance for the members who expect to claim on it, a bill for the ones who do not.

proposals.name: Strict Fiscal Compact
proposals.summary: Public debt under 60% of GDP, the treaty number, read as a commitment rather than an aspiration. Eleven of the twenty-seven are above it today, four of the six largest economies among them, and that is the point of asking.
